stories.label: Iran war / Hormuz blockade — diplomatic and kinetic arc
stories.summary: Umbrella arc for the US-Iran war and Hormuz disruption. As of 2026-05-10: Trump publicly rejected Iran's Pakistan-mediated proposal (Lebanon ceasefire + sanctions relief bundled with uranium); IRGC threatened US bases if more tankers are hit after F/A-18s disabled two; first post-war Qatari LNG transit; bulk carrier struck in Qatari waters hours later; ~100 HK ships and 2,300 seafarers stranded; Aramco's East-West pipeline running 7M b/d as Hormuz bypass driving 25% Q1 profit jump. Selector should treat new entries in this arc as confirmation/escalation evidence, not as fresh leads — only publish if the new development changes the strategic picture (kinetic escalation, mediator change, named ceasefire term, infrastructure decision). Avoid generic Trump-quote restatements or daily oil-price reaction pieces.

stories.label: Iran war second-order effects on national economies (rationing, fuel-price politics)
stories.summary: How specific national economies are absorbing the Hormuz shock. US: 3.5% inflation, Trump open to gas-tax pause; India: Modi asks 1.4B citizens to cut fuel, gold, foreign travel — three of India's largest forex outflows, 'patriotism' framing softens import-tariff signaling; UK: 1.7bn-pound BA fuel hit, halved house-price gains, wind+solar saved 1.7bn in gas imports. Selector: prefer a country's central-bank/finance-ministry signal or a measurable behavioural lever (rationing, tax pause, capital control) over yet another fuel-price headline. Each new entry should reveal a structural lever — not just price movement.

stories.label: 'Nobody will fly on these routes': Ashwini Vaishnaw says bullet trains will dominate short-haul travel
stories.summary: India's railways minister announced a Rs 16 lakh crore ($190B) high-speed rail buildout targeting Mumbai-Pune in 48 minutes — explicitly aimed at killing short-haul aviation on the route. Lead with the substitution mechanism and the political bet: a state minister publicly forecasting the collapse of a private aviation segment. Structural why: in a post-Iran-war forex-stressed India where Modi is asking citizens to cut foreign travel, intercity HSR is being framed as both decarbonisation and a fuel-import-reduction lever. Name the 16 lakh crore figure and the Mumbai-Pune 48-min target.

stories.label: Police officer, six others killed in Plateau attack
stories.summary: Gunmen killed seven people including a police officer in coordinated overnight raids on multiple communities in Barkin Ladi LGA, Plateau State. Lead with the coordination — multi-community simultaneous strikes are now the routine pattern, not the exception — and name Barkin Ladi as one of Nigeria's most-attacked LGAs. Structural why: Plateau's Middle-Belt communal violence continues without federal response, and the police-officer death signals attackers' confidence against state security. Karāmah: name the victims and communities where possible. Single-source but regional outlet (Premium Times NG) is appropriate primary voice.

stories.label: How Nigerians are coping with heat waves amid crippling power outages
stories.summary: Nigerians are facing extreme heatwaves with the national grid unable to deliver reliable power, leaving households to absorb the health cost. Lead with the compounding mechanism: climate-driven heat plus chronic grid failure equals a public-health emergency that the state has effectively privatised onto citizens. Structural why: an oil-exporting country whose grid cannot keep fans running is the textbook case of resource-curse accountability failure. Pair the heat data with grid-uptime numbers if the body permits.

stories.label: MPA injured in attack, four aides die in Toba Tek Singh
stories.summary: PML-N provincial assembly member Col (retd) Sardar Ayub Gadhi was critically wounded and four of his aides killed in a faction attack at his Dera in Chak 1, Toba Tek Singh. Lead with the four dead — not the wounded MPA — and name the victims if the source provides them. Structural why: feudal-faction violence inside Punjab's ruling-party patronage networks is rarely the headline because the casualties are the entourage, not the principal. Karāmah: count the four aides as people, not collateral. Single-source (Dawn) is appropriate regional voice.

stories.label: Roshan Digital Account inflows doubled since July 2024: banks association
stories.summary: Pakistan's Roshan Digital Account monthly inflows nearly doubled from $161M (July 2024) to $321M (April 2026), a structural shift in how overseas Pakistanis route remittances and investment. Lead with the $161M→$321M doubling and the named programme. Structural why: in a post-Iran-war forex-stressed Pakistan, the RDA is the central bank's most reliable non-conditional dollar pipe — doubling the channel matters more than any IMF tranche this quarter. Tie to the Gwadar tariff move in the same cycle if relevant: both are Pakistan policy levers pulling for hard currency.

stories.label: Govt reduces tariffs at Gwadar Port in bid to boost global traffic
stories.summary: Pakistan's maritime ministry cut berthing fees and transshipment tariffs at Gwadar Port to lure global container traffic that has historically bypassed the Chinese-built deepwater port. Lead with the specific tariff-cut number and the strategic context: Gwadar has been the under-utilised half of CPEC for a decade, and the Iran war / Hormuz disruption is the first plausible diversion catalyst. Structural why: Islamabad is pricing Gwadar against Dubai's Jebel Ali and Iran's Chabahar — a state-level bid for the post-Hormuz transshipment map. Name Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry and the berthing-fee change.

stories.label: Iran war leads to saffron price spike hitting London businesses
stories.summary: London Persian-cuisine businesses report saffron prices spiking sharply because 90% of global supply is grown in Iran and the Hormuz blockade has dried up exports. Lead with the 90%-supply concentration and the named affected commodities (saffron, chickpeas, dried lime). Structural why: the Iran-war second-order effect on UK high-street businesses is concentrated in diaspora-cuisine supply chains that no Western policymaker thought to model — a textbook case of sanctions/blockade externality landing on a specific community. Iran war second-order arc; lean in per editorial memo.

stories.label: Evaluation of functionalized graphene oxide as a nanostructured sensor for lead ion detection in aqueous solutions via quartz crystal microbalance
stories.summary: Researchers demonstrate a functionalized-graphene-oxide / quartz crystal microbalance sensor that detects lead ions in water at low concentrations — a candidate cheap-field-portable replacement for lab spectrometry. Lead with the deployment implication: lead contamination in drinking water is an unsolved problem across the Global South (Bangladesh, Pakistan, Nigeria), and a low-cost sensor changes the surveillance economics. Structural why: most lead-poisoning data gaps are instrumentation gaps; this is the bottleneck the paper attacks.

stories.label: As the low-carbon wave sweeps over China, how can urban economic resilience break through?
stories.summary: A difference-in-differences study of China's low-carbon pilot cities finds the transition raises urban economic resilience — but only where industrial diversification is already underway, otherwise it depresses it. Lead with the conditional finding (resilience effect is contingent on prior diversification, not universal). Structural why: this contradicts the donor-driven 'green transition lifts all boats' framing and gives a specific policy precondition. Aligns with editorial memo's 'lean in on African energy-planning literature with domestic first-authors' — Chinese first-authors on Chinese policy belongs in that frame.

stories.label: CII Business Summit 2026: Gautam Adani Highlights Energy Supply Chain Challenges And AI-Energy Era Shift
stories.summary: Adani Group chairman used the CII Business Summit keynote to call for India to build sovereign AI infrastructure — explicitly framing it as a geopolitical necessity tied to energy security. Lead with the sovereign-AI framing and the specific actor (Adani — India's largest private power generator) doing the pitching. Structural why: AI sovereignty is being argued from the energy-supply side, not the model-weights side, by the conglomerate that would build the data centres. Multi-source: Rediff + ABP Live. Note the conflict of interest in framing — Adani benefits commercially from the policy he is advocating.

stories.label: Bitcoin (BTC) mining pools with 75% of hashrate back open standard for block construction
stories.summary: Seven of the largest Bitcoin mining pools — controlling roughly 75% of network hashrate — quietly agreed to back the same open protocol (Stratum V2) for block construction, reversing the silent centralisation drift that has been the network's biggest unaddressed risk for years. Lead with the 75% figure and what it concretely changes (template-builder pluralism, anti-MEV at the pool level). Structural why: the biggest decentralisation move bitcoin has seen in years happened by industry agreement, not protocol fork — which is rare and worth examining as a governance precedent. Audience: technical readers.

stories.label: Robust LPV pitch control of autonomous underwater vehicle with input constraints
stories.summary: Researchers describe a Linear Parameter-Varying pitch controller for AUVs that holds attitude stability under actuator saturation — the failure mode that has caused most published AUV mission losses. Lead with the engineering problem (actuator saturation breaks stability) and the deployment context: AUV ocean-observation programmes in Indonesia, the Gulf, and the South China Sea increasingly run long missions where this failure mode is the bottleneck. Structural why: a small control-theory advance changes what surveys are feasible on a single battery. Audience: engineers, not crypto/AI generalists — frame accordingly.

stories.label: Pakistan KP / Afghan-border militant resurgence
stories.summary: TTP-style attacks on KP police infrastructure are now the routine front line, not the exception. May 10 Bannu attack (15 dead, Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen 3-faction alliance, vehicle bomb + quadcopter swarm against reinforcements) materially escalates tactics. Selector lens for the next week: lead with the alliance name (Ittehad-ul-Mujahideen) and the drone-integrated tactic, not the casualty count alone. Pair with Islamabad-Kabul diplomatic friction. Skip routine 1-2 casualty Dawn dispatches unless they show new tactic, new group, or named officer.

stories.label: Netanyahu wants to wean Israel off US military support, he tells CBS
stories.summary: Netanyahu publicly proposed drawing US military aid 'to zero' within a decade while pivoting toward Gulf-state defence ties. Lead with the numeric pivot ($3.8B/yr → $0) and the named replacement vector (Gulf ties), not the rhetorical 'self-reliance' framing. Structural why: a sitting Israeli PM is signalling that the post-1979 US-Israel aid architecture is reaching political end-of-life as Gulf normalisation creates a new patron pool — coincides with Iran-war strategic recalibration. Multi-source: Reuters wire + NDTV pickup gives the Indian-reader frame.

stories.label: Situationer: Punjab set to launch land-lease scheme amid concerns
stories.summary: Punjab Board of Revenue identified 124,363 acres of state land for immediate rollout of Apna Khet, Apna Rozgar (AKAR) — Pakistan's largest provincial land-leasing scheme. Lead with the acreage and the political contest: corporate consolidation framed as smallholder rozgar (livelihood). Structural why: in a Pakistan under post-Iran-war forex stress, surrendering state land to long-lease corporate tenants restructures rural power away from the smallholder economy that food security and KP-stability depend on. Name the Cholistan Desert tracts and the district magistrate role.

stories.label: Polish ex-minister flees Hungary to the US after PM Magyar says country won't protect people wanted elsewhere
stories.summary: Poland's former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro — accused of leading an organised criminal enterprise — fled Hungary to the US after PM Péter Magyar publicly refused to shield him. Lead with the Hungarian pivot: Magyar's Tisza government just collapsed Orbán's regional sanctuary-for-allies architecture in one statement. Structural why: this is the first concrete consequence for Central-European illiberal-network impunity after Hungary's government change. Track whether the US extradites — if not, the new sanctuary node is Washington under Trump.

stories.label: Thailand's former PM Thaksin Shinawatra released from prison
stories.summary: Thaksin Shinawatra — who dominated Thai politics for a quarter-century — walked out of prison after Pheu Thai's worst-ever election. Lead with the dual reality: he's free, but the party machine he built just lost its base. Structural why: Thailand's military-monarchy-Shinawatra triangle is rebalancing; the next move is whether the king-aligned junta tolerates Thaksin's behind-the-scenes role or breaks it. Pair the BBC and Daily Maverick coverage for cross-region read.

stories.label: Jim Chalmers' federal budget 2026: what we know so far about tax, housing, fuel and broken promises
stories.summary: Treasurer Jim Chalmers' fifth budget Tuesday explicitly frames itself around managing Iran-war disruption — Australia is the first major G20 economy to put the war on the cover of its fiscal package. Lead with the named levers (fuel-tax adjustments, intergenerational equity measures, housing), not the politics. Structural why: this is a concrete national-economy lever for the Iran-war-second-order-effects arc — pair with India's Modi rationing and US gas-tax-pause stories already in the ledger.

stories.label: US "minerals mafia" report reveals the battle with China for the next industrial era
stories.summary: US House Select Committee on the CCP published a 'minerals mafia' report documenting Chinese coordinated extraction and refining dominance across rare earths, cobalt, lithium. Lead with the named congressional finding (specific market-share percentages, named Chinese state-owned entities) — the report IS the news event. Structural why: this is the formal US legislative bid to legitimize extraterritorial action against Chinese mining operations; pair with the Pakistan FARA minerals-pivot arc. Quote the report itself, not Lowy's framing.

stories.label: Turkish Airlines jet catches fire while landing at Nepal's main airport; all passengers safe
stories.summary: Turkish Airlines jet from Istanbul caught fire on Tribhuvan International Airport's single runway, shutting Nepal's only international gateway. No injuries. Lead with the single-runway dependency: a landing-gear failure can isolate a 30-million-person country from international air commerce for 24+ hours. Structural why: Nepal's tourism-and-remittance economy runs through one runway. Track the reopening time and whether the Civil Aviation Authority's planned second runway moves up.

stories.label: Q&A: How jellyfish bycatch could be a valuable collagen source for cosmetics and biotech
stories.summary: Dr. Ainara Ballesteros (Catholic Univ. of Valencia) is converting Mediterranean jellyfish bycatch — a climate-driven fishery nuisance — into medical-grade collagen. Lead with the climate-fisheries inversion: warming has made jellyfish the most abundant trawl catch on parts of the Mediterranean; this turns the nuisance into a commodity stream. Structural why: bycatch valorisation is one of the few coastal-economy adaptations that actually scales with warming, not against it.

stories.label: Nonlinear dose-response of umbilical cord blood IL-6 to severe brain injury in preterm infants: a prospective cohort study
stories.summary: Prospective Chinese NICU cohort (Shengjing Hospital, gestational age <32w, birth weight <1500g) found cord-blood IL-6 has a nonlinear, not linear, dose-response to severe preterm brain injury — meaning the screening thresholds currently in use mis-stratify the highest-risk infants. Lead with the threshold-mis-stratification implication; this is a clinical-decision change, not a discovery. African/Asian preterm units that follow Western linear-threshold guidelines may be missing the worst cases.

stories.label: Scientists Studied 906 Mafia Marriages and Found Something Surprising
stories.summary: Network scientists analysed 906 'Ndrangheta marriages to map how matrimonial ties operationally hold the syndicate together. Lead with the methodology: this is social-network analysis of organised crime using the same graph-database tooling used on terror finance and oligarch holdings — the technique transfers. Structural why: kinship graphs are now a law-enforcement primitive. Pair the published finding with the named graph metric (centrality, bridge edges) that broke the case.

stories.label: EU Parliamentary Research Service calls VPNs "a loophole that needs closing"
stories.summary: EU Parliamentary Research Service officially recommends regulating VPNs as an 'age-verification loophole' — the first major-bloc policy paper treating VPN use as a problem to close rather than a privacy right. Lead with the named EPRS publication and the specific verification-bypass framing. Structural why: this is how blanket adult-internet age gates become blanket VPN restrictions; the surveillance ratchet moves through 'protect children' framing. Track member-state pickup (France, Germany, Italy already piloting age-gates).

stories.label: Meta's embrace of AI is making its employees miserable
stories.summary: NYT investigation with named Meta engineers documenting forced-AI workflows, output quotas, and attrition data. Advances the meta-ai-mandate ledger arc with the concrete named-employee accounts the ledger asked for. Lead with the quota mechanics (lines-of-AI-code targets, performance-review weight, named team affected) — not Zuckerberg quotes. Structural why: this is the first Big Tech case where the CEO AI bet is producing measurable engineering-org damage, not just culture friction.

stories.label: South Africa institutional accountability (courts forcing executive action)
stories.summary: Within 7 days: ConCourt ordered Parliament to convene Ramaphosa impeachment committee on Phala Phala; High Court forced gazettal of FMD vaccination scheme on the deadline; two SAPS major generals (Crime Intelligence, Gauteng Hawks) arrested for illicit precious-metals dealing; NMB metro's R25M transformer lease to Coega Steels under judicial review. Pattern: SA judiciary now the load-bearing wall of accountability. Selector lens: name the court and the order; the news is the judicial mechanism, not the outcome. Daily Maverick is the reliable source class. Lean toward more SA-court-mandates-executive stories.

stories.label: Latvia defense minister resigns over drone incursions
stories.summary: Spruds is the first NATO defense minister to lose his post over the cross-border drone war — PM Silina forced the resignation citing public trust, not operational failure. Selector lens: track which Baltic/Polish/Romanian official takes the next political accountability hit, and whether NATO formal-response mechanisms (Article 4) get invoked. Pair any future Russian drone incursion with a question about the political cost the host state assigns to it.

stories.label: Syria — Atef Najib war crimes trial in Damascus
stories.summary: First in-Syria trial of an Assad-regime security chief — Najib personally ordered the torture in Daraa that detonated the 2011 uprising. Selector lens: track each session, name the witnesses, log which other regime figures are named. This is the structural accountability story of post-Assad Syria; skip generic Syria-reconstruction pieces in favour of trial procedure or named-defendant developments.

stories.label: India ED arrests of opposition state ministers (Punjab Arora pattern)
stories.summary: Sitting AAP Punjab industries minister Arora arrested by ED — first sitting non-BJP cabinet member in Punjab placed in PMLA custody under the Mann government. Selector lens: track this as a federalism-and-rule-of-law arc, not a corruption story. Lead with the precedent (when did ED last hold a sitting state minister?) and the PMLA bail-bar mechanic that makes pre-trial custody itself the punishment. Lean toward each new ED action against opposition figures (TMC, DMK, AAP, Congress); skip BJP-aligned ED actions unless equally weighted.

stories.label: Bahrain mass denationalization of Shia clerics, infants
stories.summary: Bahrain stripped citizenship from infants by royal decree (no court), citing online support for Iran's strikes. Iran's HCHR called it 'collective punishment.' Selector lens: this is the Gulf's preferred low-visibility dissent tool. The structural story is OIC silence — only Mehr (IR) carried it; no Bahraini, Saudi, or Qatari outlet picked it up. Lean toward each new Gulf citizenship-stripping case that names categories of victim; skip routine human rights statements.

stories.label: Armenia CSTO exit / EU pivot
stories.summary: Yerevan signed €2.5B EU deal this month; CSTO meets May 26 without Armenia; Putin called Armenian EU referendum 'logical' but laid out the EAEU-loss arithmetic. Selector lens: the next development to watch is the parliamentary vote setting the referendum date, OR Azerbaijan's response. Skip generic Caucasus tension pieces; only publish if a named actor takes a procedural step.

stories.label: Ukraine — Trump-brokered ceasefires breaking on first day
stories.summary: Three civilians killed within 24 hours of the May 9 Trump-brokered three-day ceasefire (Zaporizhia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson). Mechanism: no enforcement clause, no monitor — structural feature of US-imposed truces. Selector lens: name the dead and the regions; lead with the gap between announcement and reality. Track which actors propose monitoring (OSCE? UN? neither?).

stories.label: France-Africa pivot to East Africa after Sahel collapse
stories.summary: Macron co-hosts France-Africa summit in Nairobi from May 11 — first major French diplomatic push since Sahel base evictions (Mali, BF, Niger, Senegal). Lean toward concrete deliverables (defence pact text, base agreement, port concession), skip declarative Macron speeches unless they name a treaty or a number.

stories.label: Pakistan as US-Iran mediator (FARA, defence pivot)
stories.summary: Islamabad is now the documented written-channel between Washington and Tehran (IRNA + Dawn confirmed). New $1.2M FARA contract pushing minerals/defence. Marka-i-Haq cemented the China-defence pivot. Selector lens: track each mediator move (named envoy, named meeting), each FARA filing, each minerals concession. Skip Pakistan-domestic-politics pieces unless they tie back to US relationship.

stories.label: AI agents and payment architecture (stablecoins, wallets)
stories.summary: PayPal + Google saying agentic commerce structurally cannot use bank rails (KYC, chargebacks not built for software principals). Trust Wallet + Mesh re-architecting wallets for scoped delegation. Selector lens: this is the cleanest non-speculative crypto use case in a decade. Track each named protocol (PYUSD, x402, AP2), each named partnership. Skip generic 'crypto bullish' pieces.

stories.label: Meta — AI mandate vs engineering culture
stories.summary: First late-cycle case study of Big Tech CEO AI bet outrunning product utility, cost showing in engineering ranks. Selector lens: track each Big Tech equivalent (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, OpenAI). Lead with named employee accounts, output quotas, attrition data — not Zuckerberg quotes.

stories.label: Nigeria 2027 election realignment (NDC zoning, Taraba violence)
stories.summary: NDC zoned 2027 ticket South — Peter Obi positioned. Catholic Diocese of Wukari documents 100+ killed, 98,000 displaced, 217 churches destroyed in Taraba since Sept 2025 — slow ethnoreligious cleansing Abuja has not named. Selector lens: African coverage was 7% in last cycle audit — actively pursue Nigeria primary-formation moves and named regional violence accounts. Lean toward Nigerian wires (Premium Times, ThisDay, Daily Trust) when feed offers them.

stories.label: China — democracies pushing back on transnational repression
stories.summary: Three democracies on the same day took action against PRC overseas dissident-policing — uncoordinated convergence. Selector lens: simultaneity is the legal-political signal. Track each new prosecution, named Chinese police-station closure, or Magnitsky-style sanction.

stories.label: DOJ denaturalization push under second Trump administration
stories.summary: 12 denaturalization filings on May 8 — a tool used a few times a decade until 2025-26. Selector lens: lead with annual count vs the 2010s baseline. Track named individuals, filing reasons, court rulings. Pair with Bahrain citizenship-stripping arc as the global denaturalization-as-policy frame.

stories.label: Türkiye as European defence supplier of choice
stories.summary: Belgian royal mission May 10-14 explicitly on defence/energy; Türkiye declining to back US in Iran war while courting NATO members on hardware. Selector lens: any signed Bayraktar order, ICBM/SLCM development milestone, or Erdogan mediation move. Anadolu (TR) is the regional voice; pair with European trade-press numbers when feed has them.

stories.label: Glacial-retreat-driven slope collapse tsunamis
stories.summary: 63.5M m³ rock wedge → 500m run-up wave at South Sawyer (Aug 2025; reconstruction now published). Among the tallest tsunamis ever instrumented. Hazard category not on most coastal-risk maps. Selector lens: lean toward warming-driven slope-collapse hazards with named instrumentation/reconstruction; skip generic 'climate change melts ice' pieces.

stories.label: India occupational heat exposure (rural/extractive labour)
stories.summary: Salt-pan workers exceed wet-bulb survivability threshold without protection. India's heat-action plans are mostly urban; the most dangerous occupational heat exposure is rural extractive labour invisible to municipal data. Selector lens: lean toward named-occupation rural heat stories (brick kilns, salt pans, fields, mines) with physiological mechanism cited.

stories.label: Global South energy planning — domestic models challenging top-down siting
stories.summary: Ethiopian team's wind-siting GIS+AHP+ML framework contradicts government plan; published PV fault-detection model targets the Global South O&M cost curve. Selector lens: African/South Asian energy-planning literature is producing domestic technical capacity faster than donor-funded planning can absorb it. Lean toward African/Asian first-author papers in Nature/IEEE/Renewables; skip donor-press-release energy stories.

stories.label: Tamil Nadu TVK government and Modi's DMK-Congress wedge
stories.summary: Vijay's TVK formed Tamil Nadu government, breaking 60-year DMK-Congress alliance. Modi reframing as Congress betrayal of DMK. Selector lens: track cabinet appointments, alliance arithmetic for 2029. Lead with the precipitating procedural event (cabinet swearing-in, alliance announcement), not the political quote.

stories.label: UK five-party realignment, Starmer leadership pressure
stories.summary: Local-election rout, Catherine West stalking-horse threat, Reform pressure. Selector lens: track procedural triggers (PLP confidence vote, leadership-rules amendment); skip Westminster gossip. Lead with Labour Party rule-book mechanics, not personality.

stories.label: DARPA containerized drone swarms (logistics-as-weapon)
stories.summary: Solicitation for drone swarms in shipping containers, remote-triggered. Not a weapon system, a logistics primitive that turns the global container fleet into latent military hardware. Selector lens: track which other state militaries publicly explore container-emplaced systems; lead with port-security / shipping-insurance implications, not just the Pentagon angle.

stories.label: Play Integrity attestation locking out de-googled Android
stories.summary: reCAPTCHA now leans on Play Integrity → de-googled Android (GrapheneOS, /e/OS) loses access to banking, government, healthcare. Selector lens: track named services dropping de-googled access, EU/UK competition-authority responses, Play Integrity API scope changes. Skip generic privacy-vs-security framing pieces.

stories.label: Emerging-market crypto exchanges as banking substitutes
stories.summary: 77% of Binance users in EM now (up from 49% in 2020). Stablecoin remittance vs Western Union: $0.0001 vs 6%+. Moody's: when households store wealth in USD-stablecoins, central banks lose monetary-policy traction. Selector lens: pair with Pakistan/Nigeria/Argentina central-bank moves. Skip generic Bitcoin-price pieces.

stories.label: eDNA routine water surveillance (biosecurity primitive)
stories.summary: Single Irish river scoop revealed first national chytrid detection + frog DNA + human waste markers. eDNA metabarcoding moving from research method to routine surveillance. Selector lens: lean toward each new national-first detection or named-pathogen biosurveillance deployment. Skip 'eDNA promising' opinion pieces.

stories.label: Climate adaptation as democracy infrastructure (summer election heat)
stories.summary: India 2024 election: 33+ poll-worker deaths in 45°C+ heat. Climate forcing structural redesign of when democracies vote. Selector lens: pair with any election-administration story from Pakistan, Iraq, Senegal, Bangladesh announcing date shifts citing heat. Skip US/EU climate framings; the live policy lever is in summer-election states.
